bounded_observations: The original Workbench startup invokes C:AddDataTypes before C:LoadResource and C:IPrefs in the captured boot-progress path.

A separate historical diagnostic observed a Software Failure requester reporting address error #80000003 while Initial CLI was running C:AddDataTypes; the current boot path no longer reproduces that exact command boundary.
The binary contains no source correspondence or executed command receipt.

refresh.behavior: REFRESH performs the date scan first and passes the pattern to the common scanner only when the date scan requests a refresh; FILES patterns are scanned when REFRESH is absent.

named_list_bootstrap.fallback: When FindNamedObject returns null, the command calls Utility AllocNamedObjectA, initializes the object user space and datatype list, creates the four built-ins, then calls Utility AddNamedObject to publish it. The static TagItem payload is captured below; final tag-name mapping remains tied to the original 3.1 utility declarations.
named_list_bootstrap.evidence_limit: Static control flow and raw tag values only; the public 3.1 tag-name mapping, meaningful user-space fields after offset 131, named-object reference lifetime and races remain open.
named_list_bootstrap.user_space_extent_evidence: The second TagItem carries raw tag 0x00000fa1 and value 0x0000008c; Utility AllocNamedObjectA receives this stack TagItem array at code offset 0x0568. Treat 140 as the requested user-space extent candidate, not as proof that every trailing byte is a live structure field.

public_operation_sequence: FindNamedObject(DATATYPESLIST) and create the four built-in binary/ascii/iff/directory descriptors when absent
For Workbench startup, wait for WBStartup, switch to each WBArg lock, load one descriptor and reply after cleanup
For CLI startup, ReadArgs; REFRESH scans DEVS:DataTypes then MOSSYS:Devs/DataTypes with DateScan; FILES scans supplied patterns
ScanDirectory uses MatchFirst/MatchNext/MatchEnd, one directory descent, Ctrl-C handling and exclusion of .info/.backdrop
LoadDatatype opens and parses IFF DTYP/DTHD plus optional DTCD chunks, builds a resident datatype function through InternalLoadSeg, and replaces or inserts descriptors under dtl_Lock
LIST enumerates the sorted datatype list and prints base/name pairs; Ctrl-C flushes output and reports ERROR_BREAK
ownership_and_cleanup: Hold dtl_Lock for the command transaction
Free RDArgs, IFF handles, DOS locks/objects, descriptor buffers, parsed-pattern buffers and DTCD segments on every failure
Keep successfully initialized datatype function segments resident; unload only failed loads or deleted/replaced descriptors
Reply WBStartup only after releasing the datatype-list semaphore and closing libraries
morphos320.known_source_quirk: The released source breaks after the first successful ParseIFF EOC because the source comment records a second-loop crash; preserve this as source evidence and do not silently broaden parsing without packed/guest comparison.

evidence_limits: Workbench static command analysis confirms five DataTypesList heads, a 140-byte user-space extent candidate, one refresh-date longword, and the listed candidate CompoundDatatype field offsets.

The longest-mask field, meaningful DataTypesList tail bytes, SignalSemaphore ownership, node ownership/lifetime, all descriptor-field semantics, sorting details and concurrency behavior are not fully established. The +54 size field, +14 secondary-node role, classic named-object tag names and the 140-byte tail interpretation retain provisional semantics.
No command execution on an authentic Workbench guest, output comparison or shipping/PURE/resident admission is claimed. The Workbench command observations do not close the MorphOS 3.20 library ABI.
Installed PURE/resident flags, same-segment reuse, concurrent descriptor replacement, package placement and differential guest parity remain open.
The audit does not authorize copying either original binary into a shipping image.
